Subject: Jump-box signer protocol and delta activation review

Hi Sam / Linda —

Thanks for the review session this morning. Per our notes, I put together the proposed operational flow for the on-prem appliance rollout in fully offline environments where the customer requires a physical courier and a jump-box-mediated activation. Key points in the attached manifest:

- Activation flow uses a dedicated jump-box (air-gapped network) to receive signed delta images and a tamper-evidence manifest.
- Each delta is signed by Redwood’s offline signer and accompanied by a Proof-of-Origin packet (hashes + signer cert chain) that the operator validates on the jump-box prior to activation.
- Operator access is limited to the jump-box; no admin keys are stored on the appliance until activation completes.
- Fallback: if signature validation fails, jump-box will keep artifact in quarantine and automatically notify our ops channel with a SHA512 diff.
- Timeline: courier -> acceptance window (2 hours) -> operator validation (30–45 min) -> activation (15–30 min).

Action items:
1) Linda — confirm courier SLA and handover checklist; I attached the proposed courier SLA ack.
2) Sam — confirm acceptance window is ok for your on-site team.
3) Kimberly / Jordan — can you review the signer cert rotation note and the operator PIN flow? I highlighted where KMS/HSM key references are required.

Attachments: 20260708-jumpbox-manifest.pdf (manifest + checklist), signed-delta-checklist.xlsx

If we can get sign-off by EOD tomorrow we’ll schedule the first activation window for next Tuesday (07/13).

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Customer Deployments
Redwood Inference

Quick notes from KMS/HSM side after reviewing the manifest:

- Signer cert chain: we will provide the full chain and a signed CRL snapshot (base64) inside the Proof-of-Origin packet. The jump-box validation script will check chain validity and CRL timestamp tolerance (currently set to 24 hours).
- Operator PIN: single-use one-time PIN generated by Redwood Ops at the time of courier sealing. It is printed on a tamper-evident slip and also encoded in the QR card Linda mentioned. The pin is not stored on the appliance prior to activation.
- Key rotation: our offline signer keys are kept in an HSM and rotated on a quarterly cadence; rotation metadata is included in the Proof-of-Origin packet.

All — thanks for the confirmations. Operational checklist below (finalized):

1) Courier arrival: on-site lead verifies tamper seal number against manifest and does the 30-min pre-check call with Sam’s team.
2) Operator opens jump-box portal, scans QR checksum card, and enters single-use PIN (printed slip).
3) Jump-box runs automated validation: cert chain + CRL check, SHA512 artifact verification, signature verification, and delta dependency sanity check.
4) If validation passes, jump-box writes keys to appliance in volatile-only mode and triggers activation.
5) If validation fails, artifact moves to jump-box quarantine folder; courier will remove package under "held for vendor review" unless Sam elects retention. Quarantine triggers immediate alert to redwood-ops@redwood.ai with attached diff.

We propose the test window on Tuesday 2026-07-13 at 14:00 PT. Sam — can you confirm your on-site lead for the 30-minute call? Linda — please confirm courier ETA two business days prior per your 48-hour policy.

If all good I’ll circulate the DocuSign envelope for a sign-off of the courier SLA and the acceptance checklist.

Jordan Blake
Senior Manager, Field Ops (On-Prem Deployments)
